plate_findings.evidence: A 14-year-old girl with multiple fibrous cortical defects around the knee; eccentrically located posteromedial and posterolateral lytic lesions
Direct X-ray of the knee in anteroposterior and lateral aspects show eccentrically located posteromedial and posterolateral lytic lesions
lytic lesions with a sclerotic rim consistent with fibrous cortical defect

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Anteroposterior and lateral knee radiographs of a 14-year-old girl showing eccentric metaphyseal lytic lesions with sclerotic rims, explicitly captioned as fibrous cortical defects (NOF spectrum). The lesions are marked with yellow arrows. Textbook radiographic presentation of multifocal fibrous cortical defects; classified by the authors as Ritschl stage A. B: Coronal and axial proton-density and T1-weighted MRI sections of the same 14-year-old patient showing bilateral eccentric metaphyseal lesions in the posterior/posteromedial femoral aspects, explicitly captioned as consistent with fibrous cortical defects (NOF spectrum). Lesions are arrow-marked; the same lesions are classified by the authors as Ritschl stage A. Disease attribution is strong, though MRI signal specifics are not described in the caption, so only location-based finding keys are used.

panels.figure_caption: A 14-year-old girl with multiple fibrous cortical defects around the knee. (B) Coronal and axial proton density and axial T1 weighted MR sections show lesions in posterior and posteromedial aspects of both femurs consistent with fibrous cortical defects.
